ENGLISH — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. goes

2. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

4. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

7. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

10. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

11. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

12. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

13. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

14. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

15. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.4.1 Class Reader: Main Ideas and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Writing process-Dialogues 13.5.1 Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writin and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.5.1 The Writing Process: Dialogues and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Extensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Sentences: Simple Sentences and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing –Noti and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
